steps.title: Maintain cell cultures
steps.instruction: Grow HeLa‑S3 cells in Gibco DMEM Glutamax and hTERT‑RPE1 cells in Gibco DMEM/F12 Glutamax, each supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Sigma) and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco), incubating at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until cultures reach approximately 70 % confluency.

steps.title: Label DNA with BrdU
steps.instruction: Add BrdU to the medium at 0.5 µM every 2.5 min, repeating the addition until the final concentration is 12 µM, then continue incubation for an additional 1 h at 12 µM BrdU.

steps.title: Extract high‑MW genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Harvest the labeled cells and isolate high‑molecular‑weight genomic DNA using the nCATS target‑enrichment (TE) protocol described at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmi5k4g6.

steps.title: Prepare ONT ligation libraries
steps.instruction: Construct sequencing libraries from the extracted DNA with the Oxford Nanopore Technologies Ligation Sequencing Kit (SQK‑LSK109 or SQK‑ULK001) following the kit’s standard protocol.

steps.title: Basecall with Guppy
steps.instruction: Run Guppy version 6.1.5 on the raw nanopore signal files to generate base‑called FASTQ reads.

steps.title: Align reads to hg38
steps.instruction: Align the base‑called reads to the human GRCh38 (hg38) reference genome using minimap2 version 2.17.

steps.title: Detect BrdU in reads
steps.instruction: Process the aligned reads with DNAscent version 2.0.2 to detect BrdU incorporation and produce per‑base BrdU probability scores.

steps.title: Convert to mod.bam
steps.instruction: Convert the BrdU probability output to mod.bam format using the detect_to_modBAM script.

steps.title: Identify replication features
steps.instruction: Analyze the mod.bam files with the custom R script to calculate BrdU gradients, infer replication fork directions, and locate replication initiation and termination sites; export results as BED files.

steps.title: Name files according to convention
steps.instruction: Name all output files using the scheme: first four characters indicate cell line (HeLa or RPE1), include ‘TE’ if the sample underwent nCATS target enrichment, and use appropriate extensions (e.g., .bam for alignments, .mod.bam for BrdU probabilities, .bed for fork/replication site coordinates).
